note.text:
To measure something is to compare it with a standard unit. A measurement always has a number and a unit: 25 cm, 3 kg, 40 s. A number alone (just “25”) means nothing.
Use the right instrument: a ruler for length, a balance for mass, a measuring cylinder for the volume of a liquid, a stopwatch for time, a thermometer for temperature.
Read carefully:
• Put your eye level with the mark, looking straight at the scale, not from the side (this avoids parallax error).
• If the object does not start at zero, subtract: length = end reading − start reading.
• Measure more than once and take the average.

worked_example.problem: How long is the object on the ruler?
steps: The object starts at {s} cm, not at zero.

cards.idea: A measurement has a number and a unit. “{k}” alone means nothing; “{k} cm” is a measurement.
example: The table is {n} cm long. The bag of rice has a mass of {m} kg.

wrong.explain: A measurement needs a unit as well as a number.
A unit alone is not a measurement: give the number too.
Words like “very long” are not a measurement: give a number and a unit.

cards.idea: Each quantity has its own instrument: length → ruler, mass → balance, volume of a liquid → measuring cylinder, time → stopwatch, temperature → thermometer.
example: To time a race, use a stopwatch.

cards.idea: Read a ruler with your eye straight above the mark. If the object does not start at zero, subtract the start reading from the end reading.

pick.why: Length is measured with a ruler or metre rule.
Mass is measured with a balance.
The volume of a liquid is measured with a measuring cylinder.
Time is measured with a stopwatch.
Temperature is measured with a thermometer.

misconceptions.explain: That instrument measures a different quantity.

questions.prompt: How long is the {o}, in centimetres?

misconceptions.explain: That is the number of millimetre marks. Read the centimetre numbers: 1 cm = 10 mm.

solution: The {o} starts at zero and ends at {l / 10} cm.

questions.prompt: How long is the {o}, in centimetres?

misconceptions.explain: That is only where the {o} ends. It does not start at 0: subtract the start reading.
That is in millimetres. Give the length in centimetres.

questions.hint: Read where the {o} starts and where it ends. Then subtract.

questions.prompt: Where should your eye be when you read a scale?

right.text: Level with the mark, looking straight at the scale.

wrong.text: Above the mark, looking down at a slant.
wrong.explain: Looking at a slant gives a wrong reading (parallax error).

wrong.text: Far to one side of the scale.
wrong.explain: From the side the mark seems to move: a wrong reading.
Looking up at a slant also gives a wrong reading.

questions.prompt: Each object lies on a ruler. One length is worked out wrongly. Which one?

right.text: From {a1} cm to {a1 + l1} cm: the object is {l1} cm long.
From {a2} cm to {a2 + l2} cm: the object is {l2} cm long.
From {a3} cm to {a3 + l3} cm: the object is {l3} cm long.

wrong.text: From {a4} cm to {a4 + l4} cm: the object is {a4 + l4} cm long.
wrong.explain: That is the end reading. The object starts at {a4} cm, so it is {a4 + l4} − {a4} = {l4} cm long.
